title: After a read, a late answer from before it is still kept out, however long after it arrives: the guard is the position, not a timed hold
why: A client may hold a row read for a while after the viewer reads it (a local read hold). The rule has no clock: the row is kept by its delivered position alone, so an answer older than it changes nothing whether it lands at once or after any hold has expired. A late answer from before the read (the read not yet on the server) must not bring the read row's unread back.
